name: csr-chunks
_comment: The BM25 half. One index across all studies, filtered by study_id -
the opposite of the Qdrant choice (one collection per study), and worth
being able to explain: Cognitive Search bills per service and per index
replica, not per collection, so per-study indexes would multiply cost for
no isolation benefit, while Qdrant collections are free and give a
one-command teardown. Different cost models, different partitioning.
No vector field here on purpose. The first implementation put dense and
sparse both in Cognitive Search and it failed on clinical tables: the
blob-indexer + Document Intelligence skillset gave us no control over
chunking, so header stacks got orphaned from their rows. Dense moved to
Qdrant. This index kept the half it is genuinely better at.

fields.name: text
fields._note: Microsoft analyser over Lucene: better clinical lemmatisation ('neutropenic' -> 'neutropenia').

fields.name: table_number
fields._note: 'Table 14.3.2.1' must match as one token. The standard analyser splits it on the dots and a search for 14.3.2.1 then also matches 14.3.2.10 - which is a different table.

fields.name: coded_terms
fields._note: MedDRA PTs and UMLS-linked terms from Azure Language at ingest time. Matched literally - this is precisely what the embedding normalises away.

scoringProfiles.name: identifier_boost
scoringProfiles._note: A query that looks like a table number or a coded term should be answered by those fields, not by a passing mention in prose. RRF then only sees the rank, so the boost has to happen here or not at all.
